answer_core:
I would not choose the Silva direction yet, and I would not default to the safer lab path. Treat both as live gates: Silva executability and fallback survivability.

For Silva, the danger is premature commitment to the exciting path before the constraint is real. Do not count it viable until data access, sharing terms, collaborator role, timeline, and advisor support can carry a dissertation.

For the fallback, invert the plan: ask what has to remain true at the stop date for the reversal to work. It is useful only if it remains advisor-backed, funded, technically ready, identity-coherent, and available when needed. A delayed pivot is unsafe if the fallback quietly disappears.

Sequence: advisor first, short Silva evidence probe second, committee after the data path is real. Use broad success rates as humility checks, not probabilities for this case. Do not build a finished proposal around Silva, do not run all options in parallel, and do not let fallback comfort hide the binding constraints.
expected_inclusions: data access, sharing terms, collaborator role
